frame: X along the existing rotating center axle, Y up from floor, Z fore/aft. Nominal bearing axis Y104, Z0.

expansion_pilots.status: Two smooth blind pilot bores only, reserved for future printed expansion screws. No threads, expansion screws or clips are modeled. Pads have 2 mm radial and blind-end walls.

spool_relief.note: Both plate inner faces are recessed 0.5 mm (3.0 to 2.5 mm thick) only where the spool flanges sweep: the annulus R34-R101 about the axle, which reaches down to 3 mm above the floor because the assumed Ø200 rim passes 4 mm above it. The carrier head, slots and tongues (inside R34) and the feet below 3 mm and outside the annulus keep the full 3 mm. Working faces 70 mm apart: 1.1 mm per side to the measured 67.8 mm spool, 0.6 mm at full axial float.

measured_spool.measured: Founder measurement 17 November 2026 of the actual Bambu spool: A (outermost flange faces, largest reading) and D (hub end faces next to the bore).
measured_spool.assumed_note: Bore (B), chamfer (C) and the radius where the flange face begins cannot be measured with the available tools; these come from the Bambu printable reference model radial profile (bore R27.5, flange face from about R40, R100 rim) and only bound the first fit.
measured_spool.reference_note: The printable reference model has flush hub faces 67.4 mm apart; it no longer sets any seating datum.

axle.key_note: Square drive key (17 November 2026, replacing the 3.75-apothem hex that engaged the disc by only 0.10 mm): four flats at the clip-groove root radius, corners rounded by the Ø8 journal circle. Flats at groove_radius keep the groove neck a full Ø6.4 circle, so the clip snaps the same at any key angle, and the corners outboard of the groove stay as four broad lugs for the clip. The 608 still slides over the key (nothing outside Ø8); the bearing seat stays the round Ø8 journal. key_min_engagement: the corners must reach at least 0.5 mm past the socket flats, well above ordinary print error (the hex had 0.10).
axle.tip_chamfer_note: 45-degree geometric chamfer X42.7-43.2 on the drive tip (printed on the bed): bed flare on sharp key corners or flat edges would jam the 608 bore or the disc socket. The clip-bearing lugs X41.8-42.7 and the end X43.2 are unchanged.
axle.interface: 608 journals on the printed spindle (cad/spindle.py). The drive journal square key and clip groove match the disc socket and clip; the thrust sleeves stop 0.2 mm short of each inner race.
axle.left_journal_note: Left journal is a printed slip fit (Ø7.9 against the 608 Ø8 bore) so the left 608 slides off for spool changes; the allowance needs a physical trial. The right journal keeps the nominal Ø8 with the disc key and clip groove.

magnets.note: Shared magnet spec: purchased 15 x 3 mm axially magnetized discs. The disc and outside handwheel use count, pitch radius, cups and front cover (cad/wheel.py reads it); the four anchor pairs (stand.json mount) use diameter, thickness and pocket radius.

mount.note: Founder-selected outside drive mount (17 Nov 2026): a fixed printed diagonal X outside the drive wall carries an integral axle and an extra 608; the handwheel turns on that 608. One stationary magnet per X arm pairs through the wall with a magnet glued into a matching pocket on an integral gray-frame branch. stand.py reads this for the frame branches and pockets; wheel.py for the X, wheel hub, 608 retention and clip. Anchor and drive magnets use the shared 'magnets' size. Positions: (Y, Z) about the bearing axis; outside parts measured from the container wall's outside face (wall thickness: outlet.json wall_thickness_mm, nominal and unmeasured).

inside.note: Branches fuse into the gray frame with their front face on the wall-contact plane. Upper roots sit on the rim band beside the disc's straight-up lift corridor (|Z| < 40.5 above the axis); lower roots sit on the lower rim band, lower_root_disc_clearance outside the disc's R40. Glue pockets open to the wall; the magnet face sits flush with the contact plane.

outside.note: One printed solid: hub, four arms 3 mm thick under the wheel, 4 mm magnet cups beyond the wheel's R60 sweep, the inner-ring shoulder and the 608 journal. Anchor pockets open to the wall.

bearing.source: SKF 608-2Z catalogue values (d1 12.15, D2 19.2, da 10-12, Da max 20, ra max 0.3). Retention contacts stay between da and d1 (inner ring) and between D2 and Da (outer ring), clear of the shields. The purchased 608's own lands are not measured.

retainer.note: Printed internal split ring in a groove inboard of the 608: holds the outer ring when the knob is pulled outward. Squeezed to pass the Ø22.4 bore; removable by prying an end.

axle_clip.note: Printed radial U clip, as the disc's retaining clip but with an Ø11 outer edge so it bears on the 608 inner ring only. It enters the journal groove through one notch in the wheel's lip, with the wheel turned to line the notch up.

clip.mouth_note: Mouth 6.0 across the Ø6.4 groove neck: 0.2 mm jaw snap each side (was 0.1 with a 6.2 mouth, within ordinary print error).

material: Bambu PLA Basic is a prior prototype material; no manufacturing settings or fabrication are approved for this concept.
provenance: 16 November 2026: founder requested removing the redundant rounded wall noses and auditing each printed part for print preparation. Rounded noses and their purpose-free support wings are removed; the surrounding guard lip retains the same drive-wall plane and nominal 1.5 mm gap. Both purchased 608 bearings, four printed parts, 82.2 mm wall span and 75 × 130 mm base are retained. Fabrication-mesh audit found a zero-thickness tangent rib/air-tube contact; rib inner radius reduced from 21 to 20.8 mm for positive overlap, preserving the Ø6 air bore and outside footprint. Later 16 November: a narrow guard roof with 1:1 axial growth and 35 degree side-strut sections lands on the existing legs, replacing guard scaffolding. The roof stops 0.2 mm inside the wall plane, preserving its contact face. Free diaphragm tips are capped at the existing guard-contact height. Bearing seats, base and inboard chamber-growth space are retained; comparative linear stiffness and actual slices bound this optimization. Physical qualification remains outstanding. 17 November 2026: frame replaced by the founder-directed spoked U-rim (two upper spokes, R6 junction rounds, central brace, three 45-degree rim undersides); fixed inboard bearing heads replaced by keyed seats for two removable carriers that lift out with the high-flow cartridge; the green axle/core is superseded by that cartridge. 17 November 2026: founder replaced the high-flow cartridge with a lighter printed spindle and threaded collar that clamp the spool by its bore-end chamfers; the journals, disc key and clip groove are unchanged. Independent review the same day: cone rings lengthened inboard to 3.5 mm with struts joining the full ring section, arms deepened to 6 mm, cones shortened to keep running gaps through the ±0.5 mm axial float, left journal made a Ø7.9 slip fit for spool changes Later the same day the founder required the collar to hold in both turning directions, so an integral positive collar lock (crest slots on the spindle, compliant key on the collar) replaced the thread-hand requirement. 17 November 2026: founder selected a fixed outside diagonal X (one magnet per arm, paired through the wall with four magnets glued into integral gray-frame branches) and an extra 608 so the handwheel no longer rubs the container. The holder, spindle and full-assembly axial endpoints (X-37.5..44.7, -36.2..43.2, -37.5..67.15 at a nominal 2 mm wall) and the 75 x 130 mm base are kept; the spindle, collar, disc, clip, carriers and both internal 608s are unchanged. The wheel starts 4 mm farther out, its knob is 4 mm shorter, and its 608 is held positively by printed parts only (integral lip, split retainer ring, shoulder and axle clip). Later 17 November 2026: founder reported the blue disc slipping on the shaft and asked for a reprint fix. The drive key became a square (flats at the R3.2 groove root, Ø8 corners) with a matching disc socket, the clip mouth narrowed to 6.0 for a 0.2 mm snap per jaw, and the Ø8 608 journal, groove, clip outline and all endpoints are kept. Later 17 November 2026: the founder measured the actual spool (A 67.8 mm overall, D 59.6 mm hub faces); the reference model had flush 67.4 mm hub faces, so the 45-degree cones sat 3.9 mm outboard of the real hub faces, letting the spool ride into the frame. Both rings became flat hub-face stops at |X| 29.8 with Ø54 loose pilots, the collar hub moved 0.5 mm inboard for D 54.1-61.6 clamp travel, and the plate inner faces were relieved 0.5 mm in the flange sweep only. Spindle 79.4, holder 82.2 and base 75 x 130 are kept.
limitations: Seven printed holder parts (frame, two removable carriers, spindle, collar, disc, clip) plus two purchased 608s; the outside drive adds a printed X, wheel, retainer ring and axle clip, a third 608 and eight anchor magnets.
Carriers seat by gravity only; no latch. Guide strength, carrier retention, alignment and bearing grip are unqualified.
C-seat entry requires nominal 0.2 mm jaw movement per side; clip entry requires nominal 0.1 mm per jaw. Snap force, stress, fatigue and creep remain unqualified.

The spindle and collar cones are sized to the bore-end chamfers of Bambu's published printable spool model; seat and clamp on actual molded spools are unverified, as are printed thread fit and clamp torque.
Bottom-side desiccant baskets remain to be designed.
Base pilot holes reserve space for future printed expansion screws only. No thread or expansion screw is modeled.
The magnet pocket is 3.9 mm deep for a nominal 3 mm magnet with a 1.3 mm front cover. Coupling torque and adhesive retention are untested.

Outside drive: drive-magnet face gap grows from 6.1 to 10.1 mm at a nominal 2 mm wall; coupling torque, anchor-magnet holding force, X tilt stiffness, glue retention, printed bearing fits, retainer and clip snap strength are unqualified. The upper anchors reach Y168.8, above the earlier frame top (Y128); container fit is unmeasured.

carriers.status: Removable keyed carriers; frame tongue runs in carrier grooves. Gravity seating only, no latch. Guide strength, retention and bearing grip unqualified.

spindle.status: Third candidate. Unprinted and unqualified: thread fit, collar lock, clamp torque, strength, left-journal slip fit and print orientation are untested.
spindle.boss_ramp_note: Conical ramp from the thread boss inboard face down to the shaft, angle measured from the axle, so the boss face needs no support when the spindle prints refill end up.
spindle.seat_note: Each ring is a broad flat stop face at the spool hub face plus a short loose pilot. The face lies at |X| = ring_x[0] + pilot_length = 29.8, half the measured hub-face width D 59.6 (envelopes.measured_spool), so the hub faces set the axial datum without relying on the bore chamfer. Face Ø54-62 (pilot Ø54 to stop_outer_radius); the Ø54 pilot is 1 mm under the Ø55 reference bore, a loose first-fit centring guess because the real bore (B) and chamfer (C) cannot be measured. The 1.7 mm flange keeps min_running_gap to the frame at the collar's 2 mm outboard travel, full axial float and thread flank clearance. Replaces the 45-degree cones of 17 November, which were placed for the reference model's flush 67.4 mm hub and sat 3.9 mm outboard of the measured hub faces.

thread.note: Custom printed thread (Ø18 major, 3 mm pitch, truncated 60-degree tooth) shared by spindle and collar only; not an ISO M18 nut fit. The hand does not matter for retention: the collar lock holds it in both directions.

collar.note: Hub and arms 1.0 mm inboard of r5 (17 November 2026) for the flat stops. Outboard travel 2.0 mm keeps min_running_gap to the left carrier and the frame after full axial float plus the thread flank clearance (the clamp pushes the collar outboard through that play); inboard 5.0 mm to the thread end. Clamped hub width D 54.6-61.6 mm.

spindle.running_gap_note: min_running_gap is the gap that must remain after the rotating unit takes up its full axial float (thrust-sleeve gap + 608 seat clearance + carrier tongue/groove play, derived in stand.py).

lock.purpose: Positive collar retention in both turning directions: a key on a compliant arm in the collar wall drops into one of the crest-only slots along the spindle thread; lift the paddle to turn the collar.
lock.status: Unprinted: arm strain, lift feel, key/slot wear and stop strength need a physical trial.
